newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Hysan slumps after building acquisition.
newsitem.headline: Hysan slumps after building acquisition.

text.p: Shares in Hysan Development Ltd slumped on Friday following its acquisition of the Entertainment Building in Hong Kong's Central district at a bumper price, but shares of other property investment firms rallied on the news.

Chinese Estates Holdings Ltd said it had agreed to sell the commercial and office building to Hysan for HK$3.64 billion. Ben Kwong, director of research at Dharmala Securities said the price was "very high".
Shares in Chinese Estates were up HK$0.15 at HK$9.20 but Hysan Development fell HK$1.05 to HK$27.85.

"Generally, the market kind of believes they (Hysan) paid too high of a price for the site, although it is good for the underlying property sector," said Kent Rossiter, institutional sales manager at Nikko Securities.
Among the stocks that benefited the most from the sale of the building were property investment companies.

"I think it is good for the property market," said Ricky Tam, senior research analyst at Delta Asia Securities. "So far we have only seen the residential prices moving up but we have not seen the commercial buildings increasing their rentals."
Great Eagle Holdings jumped HK$2.20 to HK$30.80.

"Great Eagle is kind of a natural comparison," said Rossiter. "They have got some office space and if the Entertainment Building can demand such a high price then Great Eagle's portfolio by comparison would be undervalued," he said.
Amoy Properties Ltd rose HK$0.25 to HK$10.80 and Swire Pacific rose HK$1.75 to HK$74.00.
Shares in some second line property companies also rose.
Tai Cheung Holdings was up HK$0.10 to HK$7.05. "It owns a lot of commercial and industrial buildings," said Tam.
Property investment group Kowloon Development Co Ltd rose HK$0.15 to HK$5.55. -- HK newsroom (852)2843 6345
